## Construction (greedy)

Let $\zeta(a)=\sum_{k\ge1}k^{-a}$, which is finite since $a>1$. Set $C = 2\zeta(a)+1$. I'll choose $x_0, x_1, \ldots$ inductively with $x_n \in [0, C]$, so the sequence is bounded by $C$.

The required inequality $|x_i-x_j|\,|i-j|^a\ge 1$ is equivalent to $|x_i-x_j|\ge |i-j|^{-a}$ for $i\ne j$.

**Inductive step.** Suppose $x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1}$ are chosen and satisfy the condition among themselves. For each $j<n$, let $d_j=(n-j)^{-a}$ and define the open interval
$$I_j=(x_j-d_j,\;x_j+d_j).$$
Choose $x_n\in[0,C]$ with $x_n\notin I_j$ for all $j<n$. This gives $|x_n-x_j|\ge (n-j)^{-a}$ for every $j<n$, so the condition holds for all pairs up to index $n$.

**Such a choice exists.** The total length of the forbidden set is at most
$$\sum_{j<n} 2d_j = 2\sum_{k=1}^{n} k^{-a} \le 2\zeta(a) < C.$$
So $[0,C]\setminus\bigcup_{j<n} I_j$ has positive measure and is nonempty.

**Conclusion.** The inductive construction defines the whole sequence. Every pair $i<j$ satisfies $|x_j-x_i|\ge (j-i)^{-a}$, which gives
$$|x_i-x_j|\,|i-j|^{a}\ge 1,$$
and $|x_i|\le C=2\zeta(a)+1$ for all $i$, so the sequence is bounded.

ANSWER: Choose $x_0,x_1,\ldots\in[0,\,2\zeta(a)+1]$ greedily, where $\zeta(a)=\sum_{k\ge1}k^{-a}$, so that each $x_n$ satisfies $|x_n-x_j|\ge (n-j)^{-a}$ for all $j<n$; this is possible because the forbidden intervals $(x_j-(n-j)^{-a},\,x_j+(n-j)^{-a})$ have total length at most $2\zeta(a)$.
